record.file_problem: GitHub repository metadata, README, and file list only; the code and linked reports were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a reproduction of the difference-in-means refusal direction using ablation and activation addition, plus causal tests and transfer experiments on additional models.
record.gate_note: The README reports behavioral outcomes for dense-direction ablation/addition, component ablations, SAE-feature suppression, and foreign-direction interventions. Classifier accuracy, AUROC, PAIR detection, and wrapper-swap measurements are not included as rows because they do not measure the refusal effect of the direction named in the claim. The README also describes attacks and robustness evaluations, but does not test whether the attacks suppress the direction or whether training against ablation improves robustness.
record.test_reason: The repo reproduces the Arditi difference-in-means direction and tests ablation (necessity) and activation addition (sufficiency) through real generation on six chat models. It adds SAE-feature suppression, a component decomposition, and same-dimension direction transfer.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Additions: the authors say Llama's gap is resolved, because a small SAE-aligned component carries essentially all of the causal effect while the dominant orthogonal remainder is inert. They also conclude that necessity generalizes across scale more robustly than sufficiency, which is most extreme in DeepSeek. Transfer is null on every well-powered comparison.
record.recipe_differences: The README says it reproduces the difference-in-means direction and tests ablation and activation addition. Its described ablation acts at a selected candidate layer during generated tokens, rather than establishing removal at every layer and position. This is a replication/tool repository; code and result files were not inspected or run.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model and intervention: Llama's dense direction barely affects refusal while a feature-aligned component has a large effect; Qwen3's top SAE feature alone has no effect but the top-15 set does. Transfer results also vary in interpretability with baseline refusal and reasoning-trace truncation.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-family direction transfer between Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B (both 4096-d) shows no effect for either necessity or sufficiency.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A refusal direction from one model family has no causal effect when applied to an unrelated family's residual stream of the same width.

fits_no_version.finding: Dense-direction projection classifies harmful vs harmless prompts at AUROC 0.91–0.99 across 6 models, including Llama, where the direction is causally weak.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classification accuracy of the refusal direction does not predict its causal efficacy.

record.problems: This is a repository README summary, not an independently reviewed full report; the code and linked results were not read or run. Some outcomes are described without numerical rates. The README itself identifies small samples, an underpowered DeepSeek transfer target, floor effects, and a Llama ablation result that failed to replicate. It does not report a general-capability check after intervention.
record.rows_left_out: No intervention results relevant to the tested versions were omitted. Classifier metrics and wrapper-swap measurements were left out because they do not measure the refusal effect named in the versions tested here.

untested.parts: Preservation of general capabilities after ablation or addition; whether ablation covers all layers and positions (README says every generated token, layer unclear). All 8-9B models were 4-bit quantized.
PAIR and GCG detection rates are reported, but there is no test that attacks suppress the direction and no adversarial training against ablation.
Affine and cone geometry are not tested; only SAE-feature top-K suppression.
No separation of harm judgment from refusal.
No cross-lingual or base-to-instruct transfer. Only one variant pair, and only necessity was tested on it.
Necessity in the reasoning model is floor-constrained and underpowered (cannot_determine). Only one small distilled model.

missing.what: Dense-direction ablation and addition results for gemma-2-9b-it (README says necessity was 'confirmed again at 8–9B scale' and sufficiency was weaker)
missing.locator: Headline findings, necessity vs sufficiency bullet; reports/RESULTS.md

missing.what: Per-model necessity and sufficiency rates for Qwen2.5-1.5B and SmolLM2 in the reproduction
Numerical rates for the DeepSeek own-direction addition null and the Qwen3-8B component ablations
Statistical test of Llama own vs foreign addition (p<0.001)

record.verdict_notes: This is a README-only read of a hobby or replication repo, not peer reviewed. Rows on transfer between different families were unlinked from V6. The component decomposition and the Qwen3 component rows were relinked to V1 only. 4-bit quantization, small n (50–75), and the classifier bug that shifted Llama's baselines should temper the verdicts. No capability check was reported.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not establish that ablation is applied at every layer and position, that general capabilities are preserved after intervention, or that additions specifically induce refusal on harmless requests. Activation-addition results are reported, but their prompt type is not stated.
No weight edit or abliteration evaluation is reported.
The README evaluates jailbreak detection, but does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
The experiments do not test affine or cone geometry directly; evidence is from component decomposition and SAE-feature interventions.
No experiment separates a harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
Transfer is reported for two architecture-matched pairs, but the second pair is tested for necessity only; DeepSeek as a transfer target is underpowered, and transfer across languages is not tested.
No comparison manipulates how or when refusal is trained.
DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B is evaluated, but its necessity result is floor-constrained and its activation-addition result is described as null without a numerical rate.

statements.problem: The natalimuca numbers are right. But the untagged 'AdvBench: 95%->29%' and the Llama-3-8B log-odds figures come right after them and can be read as this study's. The 92.0%->38.0% component result is a large drop, not weak ablation.

In Qwen3-8B each component alone cuts refusal to near zero.
statements.problem: Right numbers, but the result shows refusal carried by one small component of the DiM vector, not spread over several directions as the heading says.

statements.correction: Qwen3-8B, 50 VAL prompts: top-1 SAE feature 82-84%->84% (p=1.0); top-15 ->24% (significant from top-5); single DiM ablation 84%->8%. Llama top-1 ->10%, top-15 ->0%. Features are (layer, feature) pairs across layers. McNemar tests; no capability check.
statements.problem: The pack cuts off the natalimuca numbers. Its stacked units are SAE features, compared with one SAE feature. Qwen3-8B's single DiM direction already beats the top-15 features, so this doesn't show a second direction adds removal.
Minor: the Llama and gemma models were run 4-bit quantized. In Llama the single direction that works is an SAE feature, while the DiM direction fails.

statements.correction: natalimuca: top-15 features vs top-1 feature: Qwen3-8B 24% vs 84%, Llama 0% vs 10%, gemma 82% vs 94%; Qwen3-8B single DiM ablation 84%->8%.
statements.problem: natalimuca's 'several beat one' compares SAE feature sets with one SAE feature. In Qwen3-8B its single DiM direction removes more refusal than 15 features.
The 2048-token budget is stated in the Pair 2 design as 'DeepSeek's' budget, not for the addition test itself. Reading it as DeepSeek's standard budget is reasonable.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Qwen3-8B, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, and the reported two-small-model reproduction
reader_labels.reason: Own-direction ablation sharply reduced refusal for Qwen3-8B and Qwen2.5-1.5B, and the README says necessity and sufficiency were confirmed in the two-small-model reproduction; see r1, r4, r12, and r13.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Llama's full-direction ablation did not significantly reduce refusal in either reported sample, while DeepSeek's low baseline and null addition limit interpretation; see r2, r3, r5, and r26.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The reported full-direction ablations left nearly all refusal in place and were non-significant, including an independent replication; see r2 and r3.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Qwen3-8B SAE-feature suppression and component ablations
reader_labels.reason: The top SAE feature alone had no effect, while top-15 suppression reduced refusal; the README also says both dense-direction components independently drove refusal near zero. This is consistent with distributed or component-sensitive mechanisms; see r10, r11, r14, and r15.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Llama's top SAE feature alone produced a large suppression effect, whereas Gemma's top feature had little effect and its top set produced a modest decline, so the multi-feature account is not uniform; see r16-r19.

reader_labels.reason: Foreign-direction ablation or addition had no reported effect in the well-powered comparisons; see r20-r22 and r24-r25.
